title: A3 开源代理与 A10 基线相关性报告
method: 只读汇总 A1/A2 既有开源代理 artifact，并以 T-064 的真实 Quartus A10 full-flow/STA 作为方向参考。A3 不运行 Yosys/nextpnr/Quartus，不做任何线性换算，不新增 A10 Fmax 声明。

a1_generic_synth.note: Generic 4-LUT proxy; not an FPGA vendor resource report.

a2_soc_stub.note: Boundary stub only; no real core/cache/SoC logic.

verilator_real_soc_elaboration.note: Real lcvex_catapult_soc_top through tie-off wrapper elaborates in Verilator; warnings disabled as fatal for this lint harness.

ecp5_nextpnr.reason: 2627 port bits exceed LFE5U-85F IO capacity (365 TRELLIS_IO cells).

a10_t064_reference.note: External T-064 full-flow/STA evidence, cited as directional reference only.
a10_t064_reference.flow: quartus_sh --flow compile catapult_a10 -c catapult_a10, exit 0, 0 errors / 68 warnings

correlation.scope: Only module proportions within the A1 proxy, ranking, and qualitative trends are compared. No ECP5/Yosys-to-A10 linear conversion or derived A10 percentage is performed.

observations.text: Within A1's synthesizable proxy set, lcvex_axi4_master is the dominant LUT/FF consumer, followed by lcvex_mem_delay and lcvex_mem_arb. This is an internal open-source proxy ranking; it is not asserted to be the A10 module ranking because T-064 does not include per-module fit breakdown.

A1 proxy modules are register-heavy (AXI4 master 2406 FF vs 1870 LUT; mem_delay 241 FF vs 63 LUT). A10 real fit also shows more registers (8641) than ALMs (4468). This is only a qualitative trend; ALM and generic 4-LUT are different architectural units and cannot be linearly converted.
A1 reports DSP N/A because no device DSP mapping was performed; A10 T-064 fit reports 0 DSP blocks. There is no contradiction, but no proxy-to-A10 DSP proportion can be derived.
A1 RAM bits are 0 because generic synthesis did not map memory to device RAM; A10 T-064 uses 27 RAM blocks (including Qsys/EMIF/boot). The two metrics are not comparable.

A2's boundary stub has 109 ports / 2627 port bits, while T-064 A10 fit reports 141 package pins. The huge difference is expected: A2 counts wide internal SoC buses (EMIF/Avalon/JTAG/EPCQ etc.) as boundary ports, whereas A10 implements most of those interfaces as Qsys/internal IP and only package pins reach the board. This must not be read as an area or pin-count prediction.
A2's generic stub is 0-cell by design; it is a port/boundary manifest, not a logic resource proxy. It cannot be compared to A10 ALM/register counts.

The A-line toolchain trend is: real SoC top can be elaborated by Verilator through tie-off, direct Yosys synthesis is blocked by SystemVerilog package/import/unpacked-array ports, and ECP5 nextpnr is blocked by I/O capacity for the boundary stub. This supports treating A1/A2 as logic/boundary proxies, not as A10 QoR predictors.

not_comparable: A1 FF counts to A10 registers.
A1 0 RAM bits to A10 27 RAM blocks.
A2 0-cell stub to A10 resource counts.
A2 109 ports/2627 port bits to A10 141 package pins.
A2 ECP5 failure to A10 timing.
ABC delay (not present in A1) to A10 Fmax.

timing.a1: N/A - no timing claim; ABC delay was not used as Fmax in A1.
timing.a2_ecp5: N/A - nextpnr-ecp5 could not place all TRELLIS_IO cells; no Fmax claimed.
timing.a10_t064_reference: Recorded in T-064 evidence: worst setup +0.220 ns, worst hold +0.017 ns; Fmax values as listed above. A3 cites these only as external reference and makes no new A10 Fmax claim.
timing.a3_claim: A3 does not generate, derive, or assert any A10 Fmax.

known_limits: A1 did not synthesize lcvex_core or lcvex_l2; therefore there is no complete core/cache/SoC open-source resource proxy.
A1 generic 4-LUT/FF counts are not Arria 10 or ECP5 vendor resource counts.
A2 boundary stub has no logic and is not a real SoC area proxy.
A2 nextpnr-ecp5 failed at IO packing; no ECP5 route/Fmax is available.
T-064 A10 fit/STA is remote Quartus evidence from a different worktree/task; it is used only as a directional reference.
T-064 does not include per-module or hierarchical A10 fit resource breakdown, so module-level A10 ranking cannot be verified.
No Quartus, Yosys, nextpnr, or synthesis tool was run in A3.
recommendations: Use A1/A2 reports only for identifying which open-source-synthesizable modules dominate within the proxy set and to maintain the boundary/IP stub list.
Do not set A10 resource/Fmax thresholds from these numbers; keep T-067/Quartus as the only source of A10 signoff.
If A-line continues, the most useful next step is either a hierarchical Quartus report (not open-source) or a more complete core/L2 memory-blackbox proxy; neither replaces A10 signoff.
For A4 trend regression, limit thresholds to proxy-internal invariants (deterministic Yosys netlist/stat hash, stub port list stability), not to A10-derived limits.
disclaimers: This is not an Arria 10 signoff report.
This does not replace Quartus synthesis/STA.
This does not unblock or replace T-067.
No ECP5/Yosys/ABC number was linearly converted to an A10 resource, percentage, or Fmax.

verification.note: A3 is an analytical report; no synthesis/compile was executed.
